evidence: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:964-975 calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder inside forEach without await. The surrounding try/catch does nothing for async rejections. Still, both helpers catch and log their own errors (emailReminderManager.ts:202,233-235; smsReminderManager.ts:178,187-189), so 'errors not caught' is overstated. The real risk is that these SendGrid/Twilio/DB calls are fire-and-forget and may not finish in a serverless handler. Fix: await Promise.all(workflowReminders.map(...)).

cancelled:true is only ever set in deleteScheduledEmailReminder (emailReminderManager.ts:225-232). deleteScheduledSMSReminder never sets it; it cancels via Twilio and deletes the row (smsReminderManager.ts:179-186). So the query at scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-51 can only return EMAIL reminders, and no SendGrid call is made for SMS. Adding method: EMAIL would only be defensive.

schema.prisma:634-645: WorkflowReminder has no indexes apart from the unique referenceId. But the existing cron queries on the same table (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:34-41 deleteMany on method+scheduledDate; :80-87 on method+scheduled+scheduledDate) are also unindexed, so this isn't a regression. The table is pruned every run (past-dated rows deleted at :34), and a nullable boolean is a low-selectivity leading column. An index on scheduledDate would be a reasonable improvement, but nothing breaks without it.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:519-525 calls the async helpers in forEach without awaiting. Errors are caught and logged inside the helpers (emailReminderManager.ts:233; smsReminderManager.ts:187), so the 'errors not caught' part is wrong. The calls are still fire-and-forget: the step is deleted right after (cascading to reminders), so the SMS-path delete can race the cascade and fail. Fix: await Promise.all.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488-494: this is a regression. Before the PR, the reminder deletes were collected and awaited with `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete)` (removed in the diff). Now the update to cancelled:true and the SMS deletes are not awaited and may not complete before the request ends. Errors are caught inside the helpers, so only the 'not complete' half of the claim holds.

scheduleEmailReminders.ts:54. The repo uses @prisma/client ^4.8.1 (packages/prisma/package.json:27). In Prisma 4.x, delete() returns Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>, generated as `class Prisma__XClient<T, Null = never> implements PrismaPromise<T>`. The annotation is accurate. Inference or Promise<WorkflowReminder>[] would also work, so at most this is a style choice, not an error.

emailReminderManager.ts:213-222 is accurate: with immediateDelete the email is cancelled in SendGrid, then the function returns without deleting the row. The impact is small, though. The workflow-delete (workflows.tsx:212-224) and step-delete (:519-525) callers then delete the workflow/step, and WorkflowStep onDelete: Cascade removes the reminders (schema.prisma:643). In handleNewBooking.ts:968 the original booking is kept, but the cron deletes every EMAIL reminder whose scheduledDate has passed (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:33-41). So the rows are temporary, not permanently orphaned. Deleting the row in that branch would be cleaner.

scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56-74: the delete for a reminder is only pushed after its SendGrid request succeeds (:57 is awaited before :66). If a request throws, control jumps to the catch at :75 and Promise.all at :74 never runs. Prisma query promises are lazy, so none of the queued deletes run either. So a failed cancellation never deletes its DB row. The real weakness is the opposite: one failure aborts the whole batch, so the reminders already cancelled are not deleted.

A reminder can only have cancelled:true if it has a non-null referenceId. deleteScheduledEmailReminder deletes the row when referenceId is null (emailReminderManager.ts:203-210) and only sets cancelled:true afterwards (:225-232). The cron query at scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-51 therefore never returns a cancelled reminder with a null referenceId, and the SendGrid call at :57-64 always gets a batch_id.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376-382: this is a regression. The PR removed `await Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise)`, so the cancelled:true updates and SMS deletes are now fire-and-forget. The mutation goes on to change workflowsOnEventTypes and returns without them completing. The removed deleteMany also checked booking.userId === ctx.user.id, and that check is gone. Errors are caught inside the helpers (emailReminderManager.ts:233), so the 'errors not caught' part is wrong.

workflows.tsx:212-218: these calls are not awaited, and ctx.prisma.workflow.deleteMany at :220 runs right after, cascading to the reminder rows. The un-awaited SendGrid cancel or Twilio cancel + delete may not finish, and the SMS delete can fail if the cascade wins. Note: the email path here uses immediateDelete=true, so it does not set cancelled:true as the comment claims. The fire-and-forget pattern existed before this PR. Errors are caught inside the helpers.

workflows.tsx:574-580 is accurate: forEach(async ...) does not await the callbacks, and the callback itself doesn't await the helpers either. The outer forEach was already unawaited before the PR, but the PR dropped the awaited deleteMany inside the callback. Rejections are handled inside the helpers (emailReminderManager.ts:233, smsReminderManager.ts:187), so there are no unhandled errors. Completion is still not guaranteed. Fix: await Promise.all(remindersToUpdate.map(...)).

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:485-495: this is a regression. Before the PR, the reminder deleteMany promises were added to prismaPromises and awaited. Now deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder are fire-and-forget, and only attendee/bookingReference deletes are awaited (:495-497). In a serverless runtime the cancelled:true update may not complete, so the email would still be sent. Errors are caught inside the helpers, so only the completion half of the claim holds.
